public_rationale: The claim is that hardly anyone trusted OpenAI anymore, as of August 19, 2026. The polls from the target period point in different directions. A national poll of 1,566 voters, fielded May 2-4, 2026, put OpenAI's net favorability at -41 (e1). It does not report what share viewed OpenAI favorably. The same poll asked which company voters trust most to develop AI responsibly. The top company drew 10.3%, and 59% named no company or were unsure (e2). Because that question allowed only one choice, it shows relative trust, not the share who trust OpenAI. A second poll of 3,008 voters, fielded May 29 to June 3, found OpenAI at +11 net favorability among respondents who had heard of it (e3). That result comes from a secondary report. A March 2026 poll found 12% favorable toward OpenAI, but it was fielded before the target period and is context only (e4). No poll in the packet measures trust in OpenAI directly or dates from August 2026. No poll shows a decline within the period. The evidence meets neither the support condition nor the contradiction condition.
limitations: No poll in the packet directly measures the share of people who trust OpenAI. Favorability is only a proxy.
The -41 net figure (e1) comes without the favorable share behind it.
The +11 figure (e3) counts only respondents who had heard of OpenAI and comes from a secondary summary, because the primary report was paywalled.
No polling from after the August 18, 2026 safety-pause announcement was found.
The packet has no comparable earlier and later measures from the target period, so it cannot show the decline that 'anymore' implies.

statement.excerpt: To begin with, hardly anyone trusts them anymore, which can’t be great for business.

our_interpretation: Plain reading: at the time of the post, only a very small share of the public trusted OpenAI, and this was a decline ('anymore').
No measure was named. Representative public polling on trust in OpenAI, or the closest proxy (favorability of OpenAI), is the relevant evidence.
The X replies Marcus quotes about the safety-pause tweet are anecdotes, not a measure of trust.
Usage of ChatGPT is not treated as trust.
The aside 'can't be great for business' is commentary and is not graded.
criteria.support_condition: Representative polling from roughly May to August 2026 shows that only a small minority trusts or views OpenAI favorably, with clear majorities distrusting it.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative polling from the same period shows that a substantial share (for example, a plurality or a large minority) trusts or views OpenAI favorably.

evidence.excerpt: The AI-native challengers are deeply underwater: OpenAI at -41, X and xAI at -38, and Anthropic at -20, the least negative of the group but still firmly in deficit.
evidence.explanation: A national poll of 1,566 voters fielded May 2-4, 2026 found OpenAI's net favorability at -41, the worst among the AI companies tested apart from Meta. This fits the claim of broad public distrust. It does not give OpenAI's favorable share by itself.

evidence.excerpt: The most-trusted AI developer tops out near 10 percent, and the single largest bloc trusts no company at all.
evidence.explanation: Asked which company they trust most to develop AI responsibly, voters did not pick OpenAI. It scored below Google's 10.3%. This is a single-choice question, so it shows low relative trust, not the share who trust OpenAI at all.

evidence.excerpt: Among respondents who knew each company, OpenAI posted net favorability of +11, against +3 for Anthropic.
evidence.explanation: A second national voter poll, fielded a few weeks later, found OpenAI net favorable among the 87% who knew it. That means a sizeable share viewed it positively, which is hard to square with 'hardly anyone'. This is a secondary report because the primary page is paywalled.

evidence.excerpt: It found OpenAI at 12% favorable and 49% unfavorable, with 5% saying they had never heard of it.
evidence.locator: Section 'Favorite' Depends on Who Counts, paragraph 1
evidence.explanation: An earlier poll found only 12% favorable toward OpenAI, which is closer to 'hardly anyone'. It was fielded in March 2026, before the target period, so it is context only. It also shows how much results depend on question wording.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A representative national poll fielded around August 2026 that asks directly whether respondents trust OpenAI and reports the share who do. Ideally, a comparable earlier measure would also be available to show whether trust declined.
